Incorrigible

in-KOR-i-juh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incorrigible is incapable of being reformed.

Every teacher warned the new principal about the incorrigible prankster in seventh grade who had never once stopped despite years of detentions.

Worked Example

The shelter labeled the old dog incorrigible after it chewed through its fifth leash in a single month, but the new owners just called it spirited.

Incorrigible describes a habit or behavior so persistent that punishment and correction have simply stopped working.

How Incorrigible Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unreformable

unreformable: not capable of being changed for the better

irredeemable

irredeemable: beyond saving or correction

Antonyms

reformable

reformable: capable of being improved

obedient

obedient: willing to follow rules

How Strong Is It? — mischievous → incorrigible → incorrigible

mischievous vs. incorrigible

mischievous vs. incorrigible: A mischievous kid might tease his sister once.

incorrigible vs. incorrigible

incorrigible vs. incorrigible: An incorrigible kid tricks his sister the same way every single day, no matter the punishment.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

root+suffix — corrigible

root+suffix — corrigible: able to be corrected (Latin (corrigere))

Put it together

Put it together: in- ("not") + corrigible ("able to be corrected") = incapable of being reformed.

Use the root in a new word: correct

Use the root in a new word: correct: The same root gives us the everyday word "correct" -- to fix or set right.
